items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I worked with John Clayton, the great bassist, and he told me some things to do to tweak the settings on Zoom.

ctx.x: Right. Not through the airwaves and whatever Zoom —

I worked with John Clayton, the great bassist, and he told me some things to do to tweak the settings on Zoom. He said, “Get a mic, a separate mic, your computer mic isn’t adequate.” And all the teachers kind of got together and sort of helped each other and coached each other as to what they need. But literally, when you play a trumpet towards your computer it tries to, I forget what they call it, balance it. Compress it. So I’d be — when I first started my Zoom lessons like [scats] and it would just get this…
What about the motivation of the students? Did you get a sense of where they’re at?
